references.text: Sittim (Abel-Sittim) is mentioned as Israel's last campsite before crossing the Jordan, which is the starting point for Joshua's journey in this verse.
Sittim was the place where Israel stayed before crossing the Jordan, and this verse refers to their stay there.
Joshua sent spies from Sittim, the same place mentioned here as the starting point for the journey to the Jordan.
The Lord's command to Joshua to cross the Jordan is the background for this journey to the River Jordan.
Moses rose early in the morning, just as Joshua did here—a pattern of obedience and readiness.
Abraham rose early in the morning to obey God; the same expression is used regarding Joshua's obedience.
The prophet Micah refers to the journey from Sittim as part of God's story of salvation with Israel.
